tldr: Smith's principled libertarian case against US foreign interventionism applied consistently, including to the Israel-Palestine conflict - an argument that creates friction with both left and right audiences
The anti-war political tradition from Rothbard to Ron Paul and Smith's argument that the real political divide is war party versus peace party, not left versus right
Drug legalization from libertarian first principles: the moral case against state violence toward non-harmful personal choices and what decriminalization has actually produced in practice

Government overreach across multiple domains - from surveillance to regulatory capture to monetary policy - and the libertarian framework for understanding why government programs consistently expand beyond their original mandates
Comedy as political commentary: Smith's argument that comedians have more freedom to tell the truth than journalists, and what that reveals about how institutional media shapes permissible discourse

The 2024 election and what libertarians should do: third-party voting, strategic considerations, and Smith's argument that building an anti-establishment coalition matters more than any single election outcome
